subject.title: perf(sqlite): fast schema gates, background integrity verification, and downgrade protection

question: When a full verifier proves corruption but cannot persist its quarantine row, should OpenClaw preserve the existing full-open integrity protection until durable state is recorded, or may a restart fall back to the cheaper schema_meta-only gate?
rationale: This is a user-data and fail-closed boundary tradeoff: the branch intentionally removes the previous broad open-time scan, while the remaining durable marker lives in the database whose availability may be the failure condition.

options.title: Keep a fail-closed fallback
options.body: Retain full integrity validation or an equivalent restart-safe guard whenever the quarantine record cannot be persisted, and add a restart regression test.

options.title: Approve the process-local window
options.body: Accept that a restart may use the targeted check until the next daily verifier pass when durable quarantine persistence fails.

options.title: Defer scan reduction
options.body: Keep the previous full open-time validation until maintainers approve a durable quarantine design.

recommendation.title: Keep a fail-closed fallback
recommendation.body: Retain full integrity validation or an equivalent restart-safe guard whenever the quarantine record cannot be persisted, and add a restart regression test.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current design and recently merged adjacent SQLite safety work.
